item.title: Milvus Updates Python SDK Documentation and Development Workflow
item.description:
Milvus Updates Python SDK Documentation and Development Workflow

The Milvus Vector Database project has released documentation and guidelines for its Python SDK, outlining installation methods, contribution processes, and version management practices.

📦 Installation & Requirements

PyMilvus supports Python 3.9+ and can be installed via pip or pip3. Specific versions of PyMilvus can be installed or upgraded to the latest release using pip commands.

🛠️ Development Workflow

Local development for the project uses the uv package manager, which must be installed before running make targets. The process includes:

  • Running pre-commit hooks to automatically execute linting and formatting checks before each commit.
  • Retrieving protos matching generated files, with specific version details available in milvus-proto.

🔄 Testing & Versioning

Commits on the development branch are packaged and uploaded to Test PyPI. The package naming convention for development branches follows the format x.y.z.rc<dist>, where <dist> represents the number of commits differing from the most recent release. Installing these packages requires appending --extra-index-url to the pip command.

💬 Community & Documentation

Contributors are encouraged to read contribution guidelines before adding code. For discussions or problem-solving, the community can be reached in the Slack channel #py-milvus. Documentation for PyMilvus is available online at the project’s API reference URL.

#Milvus #PythonSDK #VectorDatabase #DevOps #Programming

Source: milvus-io/pymilvus

item.title: EasyVecDB Launches Comprehensive Vector Database Learning Project
item.description:
EasyVecDB Launches Comprehensive Vector Database Learning Project

EasyVecDB is a learning project aimed at developers and researchers, providing a systematic study of vector database systems.

🔍 Overview

  • Focuses on three directions:
    • 理论入门：理解向量数据库的原理、架构与索引机制
    • 实战教程：掌握 Milvus / Faiss / Annoy 的使用与优化技巧
    • 项目案例：从零构建 RAG、嵌入检索、聚类可视化等完整项目

🧩 How it works

The content is organized into two parts:

  • 基础学习篇
  • 实践篇

Navigation links:

  • Chapter 1 项目介绍
  • Chapter 2 为什么需要向量数据库
  • Chapter 3 向量嵌入算法基础
  • Chapter 4 向量搜索算法基础
  • Chapter 5 ANN 搜索算法
  • Chapter 5 Vamana 算法
  • Chapter 5 DiskANN 系统
  • Chapter 6 实现你自己的向量数据库
  • Annoy 入门与环境搭建
  • FAISS 入门与环境搭建

⚙️ Key details

item.title: Attu 3.0 Expands AI-Native Management for Milvus Vector Databases
item.description:
Attu 3.0 Expands AI-Native Management for Milvus Vector Databases

Attu 3.0, an AI-native management tool for Milvus vector databases, has been released, expanding the visual experience for Milvus 3.0 while retaining compatibility with Milvus 2.6.0+ and Zilliz Cloud.

🔍 Overview

  • Attu is an AI-native management tool for Milvus vector databases.
  • Connect to multiple Milvus clusters from a single instance, browse collections, run vector searches, manage backups, monitor health, and chat with an AI agent that understands your data.

🚀 Availability

  • Available as a web app (Docker, Kubernetes, or a standalone server package) or desktop app (macOS, Linux, Windows).
  • Attu v3.0 supports Zilliz Cloud and open-source Milvus 2.6.0+ and 3.x.
  • Milvus 2.5.x and earlier are not supported.
  • The v3.0.0 release includes a non-Docker, non-Electron server package for Linux x64.

⚙️ Key details

  • Explore Parquet and Iceberg data without copying it into Milvus, refresh external schemas and data, and browse or restore Collection Snapshots.
  • Work with Milvus TEXT fields, add or remove supported fields, edit descriptions, and manage Function Fields from the Schema page.
  • Run Query and Search aggregations, group and order results, paginate large result sets, and apply Function Score reranking.
  • Configure MinHash Function Fields and MINHASH_LSH indexes to find near-duplicate documents from raw text.
  • Register reusable dictionaries, stop-word lists, synonym lists, and tokenizer resources.
  • Load or release individual partitions, configure entity-level TTL, export complete Collections, and import large files in chunks.
  • The Docker image stores its SQLite database at /data/attu.db by default.
  • The -v attu-data:/data volume persists your saved connections, agent conversations, and preferences across container restarts.
  • The image runs as the non-root node user (uid=1000, gid=1000), so named volumes are recommended.
  • On SELinux-enabled hosts, also add the :Z mount option: ./attu-data:/data:Z.
  • The non-Docker server package requires Node.js 24.x and includes the Attu server bundle and bin/milvus-backup.
  • The launcher defaults to 0.0.0.0:3080.
  • Set HOST, PORT, ATTU_DATA_DIR, or ATTU_DB_PATH to customize the runtime paths and listener.
  • Connect to multiple Milvus instances from a single Attu deployment.
  • Add, edit, and switch between connections in the sidebar.
  • Each cluster has its own dedicated workspace with independent monitoring, agent sessions, and preferences, ideal for managing dev, staging, and production environments side by side.
  • Browse databases and collections, view and edit data inline, import/export in CSV, JSON, and Parquet formats.
  • Interactive vector similarity search with configurable embedding providers (OpenAI, Cohere, Jina, VoyageAI, and more).

item.title: Knowhere Provides Milvus’s C++ Vector Search Core
item.description:
Knowhere Provides Milvus’s C++ Vector Search Core

Knowhere is an independent C++ project that serves as Milvus’s internal core for vector search, integrating FAISS, HNSW and DiskANN. It can be built as part of Milvus or developed as a library, with CPU and GPU build options.

🔍 Overview

Knowhere acts as Milvus’s internal vector search engine. For users who want to use it within Milvus without modifying Knowhere’s source code, the project recommends building Milvus directly; Knowhere is then built implicitly.

⚙️ Platforms and dependencies

All Linux distributions are available for Knowhere development. Most contributors work on Ubuntu or CentOS, with a smaller group using Mac systems on x86_64 or Apple Silicon.

The project lists these verified operating systems for building and running Knowhere:

Operating system Details
Ubuntu 22.04 x86_64 and Aarch64
Ubuntu 20.04 x86_64 and Aarch64; kept for legacy reasons, with EOL by April 2025
macOS x86_64 and Apple Silicon

The scripts/install_deps.sh script installs dependencies for building, testing and shipping the Knowhere library.

🖥️ Build options

GPU support is disabled by default. Setting WITH_GPU=True enables Cardinal GPU support when building with Cardinal, or cuVS otherwise. WITH_CUVS=True explicitly enables cuVS, including alongside Cardinal, independently of WITH_GPU.

GPU builds use CUDA 13.2 for both cuVS and Cardinal. CMake prepares the toolkit before enabling CUDA, including when Knowhere is built through add_subdirectory. An existing toolkit at /usr/local/cuda-13.2 is reused. If it is absent, scripts/install_cuda.sh installs it on Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04, on x86_64 or Aarch64, and requires root access or passwordless sudo. Other systems must prepare the toolkit at that path beforehand. A GPU device or driver is not needed to compile, and the build must be reconfigured when switching CUDA versions. CPU builds do not invoke the CUDA installer.

Common build commands include:

Build Command
CPU release (default) make
GPU release with cuVS make WITH_GPU=True
GPU release with Cardinal make WITH_CARDINAL=True WITH_GPU=True
CPU with unit tests make WITH_UT=True
CPU unit tests with AddressSanitizer make WITH_UT=True WITH_ASAN=True
GPU with unit tests make WITH_GPU=True WITH_UT=True
Debug build make WITH_DEBUG=True
C ABI and Java JNI bindings with C tests make WITH_JNI=True WITH_C_API_TESTS=True
Custom compiler through a Conan profile make CONAN_PROFILE=clang14

Building a Python wheel requires swig and Python development headers, such as python3-dev on Ubuntu. A portable manylinux wheel can be built with make wheel.

🔌 Bindings and contributions

Optional C ABI and Java 11 JNI bindings expose indexes, brute-force search and named index blobs without a framework dependency. The Java bindings are documented in java/README.md.

Before submitting a pull request, contributors can install and enable pre-commit hooks with pip3 install pre-commit and pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push. They can run all hooks with make pre-commit, or run formatting and linting separately with make format and make lint. The lint command uses clang-tidy and requires a prior build. If clang-format and clang-tidy are not installed, the project provides installation instructions for Linux and Mac.

#Knowhere #Milvus #VectorSearch #C++ #CUDA

item.title: Milvus Backup: Command-Line Tool for Milvus Data Management
item.description:
Milvus Backup: Command-Line Tool for Milvus Data Management

Milvus Backup is a command-line tool and API service for backing up and restoring Milvus data. It allows backup and restore operations to run while the Milvus cluster remains available.

🔍 Overview

  • Milvus Backup is a command-line tool and API service for backing up and restoring Milvus data.
  • Backup and restore operations run while the Milvus cluster remains available.

⚙️ Key details

  • Download a binary from the release page, or install it with Homebrew on macOS:
    • brew install zilliztech/tap/milvus-backup
  • To build from source instead, run make all; the executable is written to ./milvus-backup.
  • Milvus Backup reads its connection settings from a configuration file.
  • Copy the example and update it for your deployment — Configuration explains what to change:
    • cp configs/backup.yaml backup.yaml
  • Then validate the setup and run your first backup and restore:
    • milvus-backup check
    • milvus-backup create -n my_backup
    • milvus-backup list
    • milvus-backup restore -n my_backup

🚀 Availability

  • The latest version supports backups from Milvus 2.2 and later, and restores to Milvus 2.5 and later.
  • A backup can be restored only to the same or a newer Milvus version.

💡 Why it matters

  • Milvus Backup allows for the management of Milvus data with ease, ensuring data availability and integrity.
  • It supports various commands for different operations, making it a versatile tool for Milvus data management.

#Milvus #Backup #DataManagement #AI #Database

item.title: Milvus Java SDK Splits Into Two Packages From v2.5.2
item.description:
Milvus Java SDK Splits Into Two Packages From v2.5.2

The Milvus Java SDK has been restructured starting with version 2.5.2. The SDK is now split into two separate packages: milvus-sdk-java and milvus-sdk-java-bulkwriter. This change was made because BulkWriter requires a significant number of dependencies.

🧩 Available Packages

  • milvus-sdk-java: The core Milvus Java SDK package
  • milvus-sdk-java-bulkwriter: A separate package for BulkWriter functionality

⚙️ Key Details

The Milvus Java SDK has the following requirements:

  • Java 8 or higher
  • Build tools: Apache Maven or Gradle
  • SLF4J is required for logging purposes and must be added to the classpath

Developers can add the Milvus SDK to their projects using either:

  • Apache Maven
  • Gradle

🚀 Availability

For Spring Boot applications (Java 17+), the milvus-sdk-java-spring-boot-starter package automatically configures a MilvusClientV2 from milvus.* properties.

Examples for the Java SDK are available in the examples folder.

💡 Contributing

Contributors should:

  • Read the contribution guidelines first
  • Refer to the DEVELOPMENT.md file for development information
